subject: Proposed org transition: ops & eng ownership + QBR cascade plan (draft)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: kate@catalystpartners.com, paul@acme.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed org transition: ops & eng ownership + QBR cascade plan (draft)

Hi team —

I put together a short draft announcing the proposed redistribution of responsibilities across Ops and Eng for a subset of platform initiatives (latency, reliability, cost-per-token). Goal is to get alignment before the QBR so we can present a clear ownership map and rollout timeline. High-level: 

- Ops will take primary ownership for runbooks, incident SLAs, and autoscaling policy tuning. Eng will own execution work and kernel/runtime changes that require code changes.
- A small Transition Steering group (TSG) will manage the handoffs: Laura (Ops), Jonas (Runtime Eng), Marissa (Product), Vivek (Infra).
- 6-week phased transition with canary teams, combined playbooks, and one-week overlap for knowledge transfer.

Attached: org-transition-chart.pdf (ownership swimlane), okrs-q4-worksheet.xlsx (proposed KR updates), qbr-slide-deck-draft.pptx (QBR-facing slide placeholders).

Please review the announcement text below (this is the copy I propose we cascade the week of Nov 22). I tried to keep it short for exec and manager-level channels. Request: quick comments by EOD Monday so we can finalize slides and the cascade plan.

--- DRAFT ANNOUNCEMENT COPY ---
Subject: Operational ownership update for platform reliability & cost initiatives

Team,

As part of our priority to improve inference reliability and unit economics, we’re adjusting team responsibilities to speed decision-making and reduce handoff delays. Over the next six weeks we will transition ownership for three initiative areas: latency, reliability, and cost-per-token.

What changes:
• Ops will own runbooks, incident response SLAs, and scaling policies (actions that do not require model/runtime code changes).
• Eng will own runtime and kernel changes, performance regressions requiring code work, and model variant integrations.
• A Transition Steering Group (TSG) will execute the handoff and maintain a shared tracking board.

Why now: Faster decision loops and clearer accountability will reduce time-to-fix and improve predictability for customers.

What to expect:
• 6-week phased handoff starting Nov 24 with canary teams and weekly check-ins.
• Training sessions and a 1-week overlap window between owners.
• Updated OKRs and QBR slides to reflect new owners (see attached).

Questions? Please ping your manager or reach out to the TSG.

Thanks — Marcus

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed org transition: ops & eng ownership + QBR cascade plan (draft)

Thanks Marcus — good, concise start. A few editorial points and one operational ask: please see inline.

> Ops will own runbooks, incident response SLAs, and scaling policies (actions that do not require model/runtime code changes).
- Suggest: clarify that Ops will also own post-incident RCA coordination and retention of audit artifacts for compliance (SOC2 teams will ask).

> 6-week phased handoff starting Nov 24 with canary teams and weekly check-ins.
- Suggest adding a short milestone table in the slides: Week 1-2: shadow & docs; Week 3-4: canary transfer; Week 5-6: full ownership + rollback plan.

Operational ask: Can we confirm which teams will be the canaries? I recommend selecting one Hosted API squad and one Dedicated ops squad.

Minor wording: replace "TSG" with "Transition Steering Group (TSG)" on first mention, otherwise fine.

I’m copying SOC/compliance contact internally in a follow-up once we finalize the RCA/audit retention line.

LG — Laura

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed org transition: ops & eng ownership + QBR cascade plan (draft)

Appreciate the draft. A couple of concerns from runtime engineering perspective:

1) The phrasing "Eng will own runtime and kernel changes" is a bit broad — runtime teams will still need clear SLAs from Ops for change windows and rollback authority. I propose an explicit bullet: "Eng will own code changes; Ops retains ability to trigger rollbacks and to block deploys if incident indicators are above threshold."

2) We need a short decision matrix (owner / escalation / rollback) for each initiative area. That’ll make it much less ambiguous for on-call teams during a QBR-ready incident scenario.

3) For the canary list: recommend Hosted-API-1 squad and Dedicated-Gateway squad; both have recent infra telemetry and manageable blast radius.

I'll attach a one-page Decision Matrix (pasted below) and can slot it into the slides.

On the QBR story: let's make sure the QBR deck calls out expected customer impact metrics and the leading indicators we track (p50/p95 latency, token cost delta, incident MTTR trend).

- Jonas

> On Tue, Nov 16, 2026 at 09:07, Laura Bennett wrote:
> > Thanks Marcus — good, concise start. A few editorial points and one operational ask: please see inline.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 12:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed org transition: ops & eng ownership + QBR cascade plan (draft)

LGTM from product side. A couple small asks:

- Can the TSG own a shared OKR row per initiative so product can track feature work vs ops tasks?
- Please add a line in the announcement that product will continue prioritization decisions in partnership with Eng/Ops (to avoid confusion).

If you want, I can help reword the "Why now" section to highlight customer stories and measurable metrics. Happy to take that action if folks agree.

Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: kate@catalystpartners.com, paul@acme.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed org transition: ops & eng ownership + QBR cascade plan (finalized draft)

Thanks all — great feedback. I updated the deck and announcement copy with the changes below and attached the revised artifacts (org-transition-chart.pdf v2, okrs-q4-worksheet.xlsx v2, qbr-slide-deck-draft v3). Summary of changes: 

- Added RCA/audit retention line under Ops responsibilities for compliance (Laura).
- Inserted decision matrix and explicit rollback authority language (Jonas).
- Confirmed canary squads: Hosted-API-1, Dedicated-Gateway (Jonas).
- Added TSG-owned OKR rows and wording that Product retains prioritization in partnership (Marissa).

Next steps:
1) Final checks — please confirm you approve the final deck and the announcement copy by end of day Thursday Nov 19.
2) I’ll schedule a 30-minute TSG sync on Friday Nov 20 to prepare the canary playbooks and training slots (calendar invite to follow).
3) Cascade to managers and execs the week of Nov 22; public announcement to the broader company Nov 29 if no issues.

If there are customer-specific notes (Paul, Kate) that should be included in the QBR-facing slides, flag them here and I’ll incorporate.

Thanks — Marcus

[Attachment stubs: org-transition-chart-v2.pdf (diagram), okrs-q4-worksheet-v2.xlsx (sheet), qbr-slide-deck-draft-v3.pptx (slides)]
